before.description:
On the  Go‑Checkout  page related to the  Email  and  Confirm Email  fields. When the same email is entered but with different letter casing (e.g., uppercase in one field and lowercase in the other), the system flags it as a mismatch. 

email comparisons are case‑insensitive. It should not give error message for same email address regardless it is upper case or lower case.
before.title: Go‑Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity

after.description: On the Go-Checkout page, the Email and Confirm Email fields are compared case-sensitively, so entering the same address with different letter casing (e.g. Name@Example.com vs name@example.com) incorrectly triggers a mismatch error. The comparison in CheckoutForm.tsx's confirmEmail validate rule must treat email addresses as equal regardless of casing, while still correctly flagging genuinely different addresses.
after.title: Go-Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity
verificationCriteria: When the user types the same email address into the Email field in lowercase and into the Confirm Email field in uppercase (or any differing casing) and moves focus away, the Confirm Email field shows no validation error.
When the user types the same email address into the Email field in uppercase and into the Confirm Email field in lowercase and moves focus away, the Confirm Email field shows no validation error.

When the user types genuinely different email addresses into the Email and Confirm Email fields (regardless of casing) and moves focus away, the Confirm Email field still shows the existing mismatch error message.
With matching-but-differently-cased email and confirm-email values entered, the checkout form's submit action is not blocked by a confirm-email mismatch error.

notes: Fix site confirmed at src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/CheckoutForm.tsx CheckoutForm's confirmEmail FormInput validate rule (~lines 305-309), which does a case-sensitive string comparison against the watched email value. CheckoutFormProvider.tsx and types.ts do not normalize case, so this is the sole point producing the false mismatch. Existing spec CheckoutForm.spec.tsx already exposes getEmail()/getConfirmEmail() helpers and exercises onBlur validation, so the new case-insensitivity scenario extends that suite rather than introducing new test scaffolding. Contentstack is not involved in this flow (translation strings only), so no external-service mocking boundary applies here.

notes: Openspec supplied no acceptance criteria (empty array), only notes correctly pinpointing the fix site (CheckoutForm.tsx confirmEmail validate rule, ~lines 305-309: `if (email && value && value !== email) return t("TRM774")`). I built the full AC set from scratch since there was nothing to refine, covering: the core case-insensitive match scenario (domain-only and local-part-only casing variants), the negative case (genuinely different addresses still flagged), re-validation clearing an existing error when Email is edited to match, submission payload integrity (casing as typed must NOT be silently normalized/lowercased for downstream use — only the comparison logic changes), and regression coverage for existing empty-field behavior (required-rule and comparison-skip-when-either-field-empty) so the fix doesn't accidentally change unrelated validation paths. Flagged two edge cases (whitespace-insensitivity, Unicode casing) as out-of-scope-per-description but worth a quick sanity check during implementation. All criteria are Given/When/Then observable-outcome statements verifiable via the rendered form's error text and field values — none reference mocks, imports, or specific libraries.
